title: Application factory, configuration, and blueprint wiring
description: The app is constructed by a create_app application factory that loads default config (SECRET_KEY, instance-relative SQLite DATABASE path), optionally overlays instance/config.py or a passed test_config, ensures the instance folder exists, registers the database teardown/CLI, mounts the auth and blog blueprints, and aliases the '/' endpoint to blog.index.
spec:
1. Verify flaskr/__init__.py defines create_app(test_config=None) that returns a configured Flask app built with instance_relative_config=True. The default config MUST harden the signed session cookie: SESSION_COOKIE_HTTPONLY=True and SESSION_COOKIE_SAMESITE="Lax", plus SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE sourced from config (default False so the dev server/tests work over plaintext HTTP, overridable to True in instance/config.py for production HTTPS). Do NOT leave these cookie flags unset — that was security finding S3.
2. Verify default config sets DATABASE to a path inside app.instance_path (flaskr.sqlite) and that the instance folder is created via os.makedirs(exist_ok=True).
3. Verify config resolution: with test_config=None it loads instance/config.py silently; when a test_config mapping is passed it is applied via app.config.update.
4. Verify both blueprints are registered (auth.bp, blog.bp) and db.init_app(app) is called so the DB teardown and init-db CLI are attached.
5. Verify url_for('index') resolves to the blog index (app.add_url_rule('/', endpoint='index')).
6. Verify create_app registers an @app.after_request handler that sets baseline security headers on EVERY response: X-Content-Type-Options=nosniff, X-Frame-Options=DENY, Referrer-Policy=no-referrer, and Content-Security-Policy=default-src 'self'; Strict-Transport-Security (max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains) MUST be gated to secure/HTTPS requests only so it is not sent over the plaintext dev server. Do NOT leave responses without these headers — that was security finding S5.
7. Verify tests/test_factory.py exercises the factory (test_config override) and asserts the security headers are present on GET '/'. Do NOT wire a GET /hello (or any other unconditional diagnostic/demo) route into create_app — it was removed as security finding S6; the factory must not expose debug endpoints in production.
notes: Backfilled by feature-coverage-audit from current implementation evidence on 2026-07-03. Documents shipped, test-passing behavior (24 passed). NOTE: the default SECRET_KEY="dev" and the /hello debug route are known security findings (S1, S6 in .aidd/assertions.md) tracked separately; this coverage record describes current behavior, not the desired hardened state.
